title: Norway-Denmark
capsule: In 1046–1056 there was no lasting Norway–Denmark state; the label reflects a contested dynastic union centred on the Norwegian crown. Magnus the Good (Magnús góði) ruled Norway and, after Harthacnut's death in 1042, was also elected king of Denmark, briefly joining the two realms; in 1046 he was forced to share Norway with his uncle Harald Hardrada (Haraldr Sigurðarson / Harald Sigurdsson). When Magnus died in 1047, Harald became sole king of Norway but Denmark passed to Sweyn II Estridsson (Sven Estridsen), and Harald's claim to it dissolved the union. From 1048 Harald waged almost yearly campaigns against Sweyn — sacking Hedeby in 1049 and winning the naval Battle of Niså in 1062 — yet never held Denmark, and the two kingdoms made an unconditional peace in 1064 with their existing borders intact.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Core territorial extents in Scandinavia are well-documented through administrative records and the chain of peace treaties. Overseas territories (Iceland, Faroe Islands, Greenland, and colonial possessions in the Caribbean) are tracked in Danish crown records; boundaries on the Scandinavian Peninsula reflect treaty lines whose surveying precision varies by period.
